metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art scene-index — the case at art:92-95 that wraps `python3 runtime/scripts/build_scene_index.py runtime/remotion/src --todo`. THE LAW: 'a scene is usable only if Root.tsx declares a <Composition> for it.' The tool parses Root.tsx (banners, <Folder>, <Composition>), follows the import map to each backing file, extracts each component's own header comment (or DERIVES search text from file evidence when no header exists), and writes runtime/remotion/src/scenes.json + SCENE-DOC-TODO.md. Current isolated toolkit inventory: 620 renderable compositions, 118 undocumented (running on derived search text), 0 unresolved (every registered id has a backing file). Falsifiability beat: a scratch toolkit with two .tsx files in scenes/ but only one <Composition> in Root.tsx — the orphan is invisible until Root.tsx registers it. Recovery: add the <Composition>, re-run scene-index. Unlike ./art scenes there are no aliases: the dispatcher case matches only 'scene-index'. All demo output in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim from this workspace against the isolated toolkit's scenes.json. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. No paid API, no upload, no network calls. episode.source_sha256 6704da9d0dd6f4517ac246db700876b03934a0410af843cbe8e3bf0eefc97c9f.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI cold open. Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Bonjour, this is Liam, in for Bear. Six hundred and twenty renderable compositions live in Brutalist. Art scenes searches that index. Art scene-index writes it. When you add a component to Root dot tsx, the search cannot see it until you re-index. This is the tool that closes that loop.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — Beat 2 BLUF, written by the hesitant writer. Corrects the reel's actual misconception.
beats.narration_text: Watch the writer walk this back. Art scene-index does not read the scenes for you. It reads Root dot tsx and rewrites the index that art scenes searches. Search reads the index. Scene-index writes it. That is the whole distinction this reel turns on.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the dispatcher case. One case branch, one exec, no aliases.
beats.narration_text: The dispatcher is one case in the art file. The pattern matches only the exact string scene-index — there are no aliases. It execs the python builder against runtime slash remotion slash src, with the todo flag baked in so SCENE-DOC-TODO markdown is always regenerated alongside scenes dot json. Every argument you add lands after the flag.

props.title: art:92-95 — one branch, no aliases
props.code:
# From the top-level art dispatcher:
case "$cmd" in
  # ...
  scene-index)
    exec python3 "$ART_HOME/runtime/scripts/build_scene_index.py" \
      "$ART_HOME/runtime/remotion/src" --todo "$@"
    ;;
  # ...
esac

# The wrapper always: (1) points at runtime/remotion/src,
# (2) passes --todo so SCENE-DOC-TODO.md is always regenerated,
# (3) forwards "$@" so extra flags fall through untouched.
props.sparkLine: One case. No aliases. --todo is baked in.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — THE LAW: registered wins. A .tsx without a <Composition> is invisible.
beats.narration_text: Here is the law the tool exists to enforce. A scene is usable only if Root dot tsx declares a Composition for it. A dot tsx file sitting in scenes slash is not enough — several exist that no Composition references, and they are invisible to the pipeline. So the index is generated from Root dot tsx for that exact reason. Registered is the only truth. Everything else in the folder is a draft.

props.title: build_scene_index.py — the doctrine at the top
props.code:
# THE LAW: a scene is usable only if Root.tsx declares a
#          <Composition id="..."> for it. A .tsx file in scenes/
#          is NOT enough - several exist that no composition
#          references, and they are invisible to the pipeline.
#          This index is generated from Root.tsx for that reason:
#          REGISTERED IS THE ONLY TRUTH.
#
# THE INDEX IS THE SEARCH SURFACE. scene_search.py can only find
# a scene through the text stored here, so this script's job is
# to carry as much of the component's own account of itself as
# possible - imports, header, props, synonyms.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — how it reads Root.tsx: import map + composition scan + header extraction.
beats.narration_text: Three passes over Root dot tsx. Pass one builds the import map — local name to module path and exported name — so a Composition tag can be resolved to its backing file. Pass two walks the file linearly, tracking banner comments, folder open and close tags, and every Composition span. Pass three opens each backing file and reads the component's own header comment. If there is no header, the entry is derived — from the id, the folder, the props, and the strings the component ships with — and the tool marks it derived so search knows to trust it less.

show.event: card in; title reads 'build_scene_index.py — three passes'

props.title: build_scene_index.py — three passes over Root.tsx
props.code:
# 1. IMPORT MAP  (local name -> module, exported name)
#    import {A, B as C} from './scenes/Foo'
#    import D          from './Bar'
#    -> imports = {'A': ('scenes/Foo','A'),
#                  'C': ('scenes/Foo','B'),
#                  'D': ('Bar','D')}

# 2. COMPOSITION SCAN  (linear walk; folders open/close)
#    <Folder name="...">   <Composition id="..." component={...}
#                          width={...} height={...} />
#    -> comps[]: id, component, folder, group, w, h, chunk

# 3. HEADER EXTRACTION  (the component's own account of itself)
#    /** Name - one honest sentence. Use it for X. */
#    -> desc, when, synonyms  (desc_source: 'header')
#    if no header -> derive from id + folder + props + copy
#       (desc_source: 'derived', documented: false)
props.sparkLine: Imports. Compositions. Headers. In that order.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — the actual output line, verbatim.
beats.narration_text: So the bare invocation. Dot slash art scene-index. It runs, it prints two lines and exits zero. Six hundred and twenty renderable compositions. One hundred and eighteen of them are running on derived search text. Zero unresolved — every registered id has a backing file on disk. Two files change on disk: scenes dot json under runtime slash remotion slash src, and SCENE-DOC-TODO markdown at the repo root.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — a documented entry vs a derived entry, side by side.
beats.narration_text: Two records from the same file. On the left, a documented entry — ClaudeComposerAsk. Its desc is the opening of its own header, its props are read from its zod schema, its synonyms are mined from the header body. Documented is true. On the right, a derived entry — CodexComposerAsk. No header in the component, so the desc is assembled from evidence: the id, the folder it was registered under, keywords, on-screen strings, and the props. Documented is false. The two are equal citizens for search — but the derived one is worth reading the file before you trust it.

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — SCENE-DOC-TODO.md, the backfill ledger written by --todo.
beats.narration_text: The second file the tool writes is SCENE-DOC-TODO markdown. That is the backfill ledger — every scene running on derived text, one row apiece, with the file path and the folder it lives under. One hundred and eighteen rows, nineteen percent of the six hundred and twenty. Each row is a small chore: open the file, add one honest sentence at the top, re-run scene-index. The pile shrinks by one, the search text sharpens by one component.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — the orphan .tsx. Two files in scenes/, one <Composition> in Root.tsx — the tool sees one. Recovery in the same beat.
beats.narration_text: And here is the law in flight. A scratch toolkit with two files in scenes slash: ClaudeComposerAsk and OrphanNewScene. Only one Composition tag in Root dot tsx. Scene-index runs, reports one renderable, and puts only the registered id in scenes dot json. The orphan is invisible. Now add the missing Composition to Root dot tsx and re-run. Count jumps to two. Both ids present. The tool did not silently accept the disk file — it accepted the registered Composition. Recovery is one edit and one re-run.

show.event: card in; title reads 'the orphan scene — invisible until registered'

props.title: the orphan scene   (falsifiability demo)
props.code:
$ ls src/scenes
  ClaudeComposerAsk.tsx     OrphanNewScene.tsx    # two files

$ grep -c '<Composition' src/Root.tsx
  1                                                # one registration

$ ./art scene-index      # (against this scratch toolkit)
  scenes.json - 1 renderable, 0 undocumented, 0 unresolved
  ids: ['ClaudeComposerAsk']                      # orphan is invisible

# ------------------------- RECOVERY ------------------------

$ edit src/Root.tsx    # add <Composition id="OrphanNewScene" .../>
$ grep -c '<Composition' src/Root.tsx
  2

$ ./art scene-index
  scenes.json - 2 renderable, 0 undocumented, 0 unresolved
  ids: ['ClaudeComposerAsk', 'OrphanNewScene']    # now visible
props.sparkLine: A .tsx on disk is a draft. A Composition is truth.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface. One line each, in the order you actually use it.
beats.narration_text: So the surface. Bare art scene-index re-reads Root dot tsx and writes two files. Scenes dot json — the six hundred and twenty entry index that art scenes searches. SCENE-DOC-TODO markdown — the one hundred and eighteen entry backfill list from the todo flag baked into the wrapper. There are no aliases; the dispatcher matches only scene-index. And the law under all of it: a scene is renderable only if Root dot tsx declares a Composition for it. A file on disk is a draft. Root dot tsx is the truth.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code from the brutalist toolkit root. It exercises the full loop: run scene-index once as a baseline, count what you have, add a fresh Composition to Root dot tsx for a component you are about to author, re-run, and confirm the count went up by exactly one. Then open SCENE-DOC-TODO markdown, pick one row, add a one-sentence header to that file, re-run, and confirm the undocumented number went down by one. If either move surprises you — the count did not change, a name went missing — that is a lead: either Root dot tsx did not save, or the import path does not match.
